title: NK6410 BGT corn (NK6410): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: NK6410 BGT corn: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: NK6410 BGT corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety for Luzon and Mindanao. 103 to 113 days to harvest, 11 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: NK6410 BGT corn is a yellow GM hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as NK6410 or NK6410BtGT. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2021 as NSIC 2021 GMCn 78. Syngenta Crop Protection AG bred it. It takes 103 to 113 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain, with 11 tonnes per hectare in the trials (11.19 in Luzon, 10.89 in Mindanao).

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NK6410 or NK6410BtGT, this is the same corn. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

items: **Days to harvest:** 103 to 113 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain.
**Yield:** 11 tonnes per hectare in the trials (11.19 in Luzon, 10.89 in Mindanao).
**Plant height:** about 237.5 cm.
**Recommended for:** Luzon and Mindanao.
**Type:** Yellow GM hybrid.

blocks.text: Key facts about NK6410 BGT corn

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

NK6410 BGT corn takes 103 to 113 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. That is about the average of the 89 yellow GM hybrid corn varieties with a day count, 105.4 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 11 t/ha beats the average of its group, 8.13. It sits in the top quarter of its group. One tonne of shelled corn fills about 20 sacks of 50 kilograms. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 100 to 105 days after planting (sold as early maturing, about 15 to 20 days ahead of others), 103 to 113 in NSIC trials.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer).

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its ears grew about 18 cm long in the trials. The shelling recovery was 78 percent, the share of the ear weight that comes off as grain. A higher share means more grain from every sack of ears.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** Potential 12 t/ha, 12.6 t/ha and 11.5 t/ha at the Region 2 derby, NSIC trials averaged 11.19 t/ha Luzon and 10.89 Mindanao.
**Traits in the seed:** BGT stack Bt11 x TC1507 x GA21: built in protection against corn borer and other caterpillars plus glyphosate tolerance.
**Season:** Wet and dry season.
**Where:** Cagayan Valley (lower vega), Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, Southern Luzon, Bicol Region and low elevation Mindanao.
Early maturing.
Fair drought tolerance.
Good standability, resists lodging.
Heavy, deep yellow orange 'Class A' grain.
Easy to dehusk and harvest.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: won the DA Bicol corn derby in Camarines Sur, where the provincial report said many farmers there already plant it, third at the Region 2 derby in 2017 and top 3 again in 2019, on the City of Ilagan's list of common hybrids. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual corn on the same ground.
Where and when to plant NK6410 BGT corn

The registry recommends it for Luzon and Mindanao. Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is NK6410 the same as NK6410 BGT?
items.a: Yes. NK6410 is another name for NK6410 BGT, registered as NSIC 2021 GMCn 78. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 103 to 113 days from planting to the harvest of dry grain. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 11 tonnes per hectare in the trials (11.19 in Luzon, 10.89 in Mindanao). Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.
The registry recommends it for Luzon and Mindanao. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of NK6410 BGT?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
